comments.note: @types/node was absent from the devDependencies in package.json (should have been added in WP-001). Any future WP touching Node.js built-ins would have hit the same TS2307 / TS2304 errors. Added it here as part of this WP's fix.

The FolderConfig interface (and by extension the AppConfig fields in WP-005) uses PascalCase property names (StorageFolder, ProjectsFolder) rather than the TypeScript-idiomatic camelCase. This is inconsistent with standard TS conventions. If the intent is JSON key-fidelity, that should be documented; otherwise consider renaming to storageFolder / projectsFolder before more code depends on these names.

getToolRoot() is called once per exported function but always returns the same value. Caching the result at module load time (or via a lazily-initialised module-level variable) would avoid repeated filesystem walks in batch operations where these helpers are called in a loop.

summary: Build passes cleanly (tsc exits 0, no warnings).
All 4 acceptance criteria verified from /tmp to confirm cwd-independence.
AC1: getToolRoot() correctly walks up __dirname to find package.json, returning the tool root regardless of cwd.
AC2: getConfigPath() returns <toolRoot>/config.json via path.join.
AC3: getStorageFolder/getProjectsFolder resolve relative paths against tool root and pass absolute paths through unchanged.
AC4: No hardcoded path separators — all construction uses path.join()/path.resolve().
Regression: dist/index.js entry point unaffected.
Edge cases tested: empty string, nested relatives, path traversal (normalised by path.resolve, no crash), compiled entry point.

comments.note: Path traversal sequences (e.g., '../') in StorageFolder/ProjectsFolder config values are silently normalised by path.resolve, which can produce paths outside the tool root. Since config is user-controlled, this is acceptable for a dev tool, but worth noting if config values ever come from untrusted sources.

No automated test suite exists yet for this module. All verification was done via ad-hoc node invocations. A formal test file (e.g., tests/utils/paths.test.ts) would make regression detection faster in future WPs.
No observations beyond existing Developer comments — code is clean and logic is correct.

summary: Reviewed src/utils/paths.ts against all four acceptance criteria — all met.

Applied Fix-Forward: renamed FolderConfig interface properties from PascalCase (StorageFolder, ProjectsFolder) to camelCase (storageFolder, projectsFolder). No callers existed outside paths.ts so the rename is non-behavioral. Prevents the naming debt from spreading to WP-005 (AppConfig).
Build verified clean after fix (tsc exits 0).
Logic is correct: getToolRoot() walk-up is safe (terminates at filesystem root), path.isAbsolute guard is correct, all construction uses path.join/path.resolve.
Noted improvement opportunity: cache getToolRoot() result at module load time to avoid repeated filesystem walks in batch operations. Low priority — deferred to future WP.

comments.note: Renamed FolderConfig.StorageFolder → storageFolder and FolderConfig.ProjectsFolder → projectsFolder (and updated destructuring in both functions). TypeScript interfaces use camelCase by convention; PascalCase properties are unusual and would have become naming debt once WP-005 adds AppConfig composed over FolderConfig. Fix is non-behavioral — no external callers exist. Build passes.

getToolRoot() performs a synchronous filesystem walk on every call. In batch operations where getStorageFolder/getProjectsFolder are invoked in a loop, this causes repeated disk reads for an invariant value. A module-level cached variable (`let _toolRoot: string | undefined`) computed lazily on first call would eliminate the overhead. Deferred — low impact at current scale.

[documentation-forward] paths.ts exports FolderConfig interface — the Documentation agent should add a usage note clarifying that storageFolder/projectsFolder accept both relative paths (resolved against tool root) and absolute paths (passed through). This is non-obvious and will be consumed by WP-005 AppConfig and future callers.
